<a id="event-2017-02-11-1-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Over 70,000 people are evacuated from Thessaloniki, Greece, as authorities attempt to defuse a World War II-era unexploded ordnance, which was discovered last week.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/11/unexploded-ww2-bomb-prompts-huge-thessaloniki-greece-evacuation>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-02-11-2-2"></a>

Context: 2017 elections in India / Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly election.

**Archived source account.** Voters in Uttar Pradesh cast ballots in Phase 1 of the state's 2017 elections, with Phase 7, the final poll, to be held on 8 March. This will be an important test of India's November policy change that removed 86 percent of the cash then in circulation.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-election-idUSKBN15P2SN>).

<a id="event-2017-02-11-2-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Violence erupts at a protest rally in Baghdad, Iraq, killing at least four protesters and one police officer. Thousands of supporters of Shia cleric Muqtada al-Sadr gathered in the capital to demand an overhaul of the country's electoral system.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/protesters-killed-violence-grips-baghdad-rally-170211140644671.html>).

The warning comes amidst "unprecedented" fire conditions across the region, deemed to be worse than the conditions precipitating the 2009 Black Saturday bushfires in Victoria.

Context: 2017 Oroville Dam crisis.

<a id="event-2017-02-14-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Cigna announces that it has terminated its merger with Anthem, a deal that was blocked by a U.S. federal judge last week. In addition, Cigna sues Anthem for the $1.85 billion reverse termination fee, and for more than $13 billion in additional damages. Anthem says Cigna has no right to terminate the merger, a deal which in January was extended to April 30, 2017.

Source citations (as archived): [Bloomberg](<https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-02-14/cigna-sues-anthem-after-ending-their-merger-agreement>); [CNBC](<https://www.cnbc.com/2017/02/14/cigna-terminates-merger-with-anthem-sues-for-fee-damages.html>).

Source citations (as archived): [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/china-suspends-north-koreas-coal-imports-striking-at-regimes-financial-lifeline/2017/02/18/8390b0e6-f5df-11e6-a9b0-ecee7ce475fc_story.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-18-1-3"></a>

Context: War in Donbass.

**Archived source account.** At the Munich Security Conference, a truce between Russian-backed separatists and the Ukrainian army, per the Minsk Protocol, takes effect Monday. Pending a permanent political agreement, Russian President Vladimir Putin orders that civil registration documents issued in separatist-held areas of Donetsk and Luhansk in eastern Ukraine be temporarily recognized. Ukrainian authorities say this violates provisions in the Minsk agreement. This is the third such agreement because the previous two in 2014 and 2015 were violated. Low-level fighting and artillery fire never fully stopped.

Context: 2017 South Sudan famine.

**Archived source account.** The World Food Programme (WFP) and other United Nations agencies declare that there is a famine in parts of Unity State, South Sudan, with 100,000 facing starvation and another million on the brink of famine.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2017/feb/20/famine-declared-in-south-sudan>); [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/famine-declared-part-south-sudan-unity-state-170220081516802.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-20-3-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Severe storms, from the weather system that hit Southern California Friday, reach southwest Texas injuring several people and damaging at least 100 homes with one confirmed tornado in San Antonio. Heavy rains continue today with flash floods likely as the storm moves to eastern Texas and southern Louisiana.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://www.usatoday.com/story/weather/2017/02/20/tornado-san-antonio-texas-storms/98149254/>); [Weather Channel](<https://weather.com/news/news/severe-weather-texas-impacts>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-02-20-4-1"></a>

Context: Malaysia–North Korea relations, Death of Kim Jong-nam.

**Archived source account.** Malaysia recalls its ambassador from North Korea amid an ongoing dispute over the alleged assassination of Kim Jong-nam by North Korean agents in the country.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-39024570>).

<a id="event-2017-02-20-4-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, the global transfer of weapons between 2012 and 2016 has been higher than any other five-year period since the end of the Cold War, with the Middle East increasing its weapon imports by 212%, second only to India, who accounted for 13% of the world's imports.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/20/global-arms-weapons-trade-highest-point-since-cold-war-era>).

<a id="event-2017-02-20-4-4"></a>

Context: Montenegro–Russia relations.

**Archived source account.** A Montenegrin prosecutor accuses Russian authorities of being involved in the October 2016 coup plot in order to halt Montenegro's accession to NATO. Russian officials dismiss the allegations as "absurd."

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/20/russian-state-bodies-attempted-a-coup-in-montenegro-says-prosecutor>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-02-20-5-1"></a>

Context: Antisemitism in the United States.

**Archived source account.** The Ronald Gardenswartz Jewish Community Center in Albuquerque, New Mexico is evacuated for the second time this year following a bomb threat, after a wave of threats against Jewish institutions in the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [Albuquerque Journal](<https://www.abqjournal.com/953557/jewish-community-center-evacuated-for-second-time-in-three-weeks.html>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-02-20-6-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Russia's Permanent Representative to the United Nations Vitaly Churkin dies suddenly in New York City. He would have turned 65 on Tuesday.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-un-churkin-idUSKBN15Z1UU>); [New York Daily News](<http://www.nydailynews.com/new-york/russian-ambassador-vitaly-churkin-dies-nyc-heart-attack-article-1.2977372>).

<a id="event-2017-02-20-6-2"></a>

Context: Formation of Donald Trump's cabinet.

**Archived source account.** President Donald Trump names United States Army Lt. General H. R. McMaster as National Security Advisor and says that U.S. Lt. Gen. Keith Kellogg, who has been the acting NSA, will remain as the NSC's Chief of Staff.

Source citations (as archived): [Fox News](<http://www.foxnews.com/politics/2017/02/20/trump-selects-lt-gen-h-r-mcmaster-as-national-security-adviser.html>).

### 2017-02-21

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1256519658](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20February%2021&oldid=1256519658>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-02-21-0-1"></a>

Context: War in North-West Pakistan.

**Archived source account.** Multiple suicide bombers kill at least six people near a district court in Charsadda. Jamaat-ul-Ahrar claimed responsibility for the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/explosions-rocks-district-courts-charsadda-170221070524712.html>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2017-02-21-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** British journalist Milo Yiannopoulos resigns from his post as technology editor at Breitbart news, after controversy around his statements regarding underage sex.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-39043496>).

#### Business and economy

<a id="event-2017-02-21-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Verizon Communications agrees to buy the core business at Yahoo Inc. for $4.48 billion. Completion of this July 2016 deal had been delayed because of two data breaches Yahoo disclosed last year.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yahoo-m-a-verizon-idUSKBN1601EK>).

<a id="event-2017-02-21-2-2"></a>

Context: Restaurant Brands International.

**Archived source account.** The parent company of Burger King announces plans to purchase Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen, operator of the Popeyes chicken restaurant chain in a US$1.8 billion deal.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2017/02/21/burger-king-popeyes-tim-hortons/98189186/>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2017-02-21-3-1"></a>

Context: 2017 Essendon Airport Beechcraft King Air crash.

**Archived source account.** A charter plane crashes into a Direct Factory Outlets shopping centre in Melbourne, Australia, shortly after taking off from Essendon Airport, killing the five people on board.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News Australia](<http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-02-21/essendon-airport-emergency/8288964>).

<a id="event-2017-02-21-3-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Flooding occurs across parts of Indonesia, including the capital Jakarta, due to torrential downpours over the last few days. Thousands of homes have been flooded and schools were forced to close. However, there are no reports of injuries yet.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/indonesia-widespread-flooding-hits-jakarta-170221104750422.html>).

#### Health

<a id="event-2017-02-21-4-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** More than 4.9 million people in South Sudan are in need of aid due to a famine.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://www.cnn.com/2017/02/20/africa/south-sudan-famine/index.html>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-02-21-5-1"></a>

Context: France–Lebanon relations.

**Archived source account.** French National Front presidential candidate Marine Le Pen leaves before her scheduled meeting in Beirut with Lebanon's top Sunni Muslim religious leader, Grand Mufti Abdellatif Deryan, following her refusal to accept the offered headscarf to cover her hair. Le Pen's aides had been informed earlier about the traditional, religious need for a headscarf for this meeting.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-election-lepen-idUSKBN1600R6>); [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/marine-le-pen-stirs-headscarf-controversy-lebanon-170221150240682.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-02-21-6-1"></a>

Context: 2017 Rinkeby riots.

**Archived source account.** After Swedish police arrest a suspect on drug-related charges, rioting occurs in Rinkeby, a suburb of the Swedish capital Stockholm.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://www.cnbc.com/2017/02/21/overnight-riots-in-predominately-immigrant-stockholm-suburb.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-21-6-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** An Austrian court grants a United States request to extradite Ukrainian businessman Dmytro Firtash. U.S. officials accuse Firtash of being involved in a scandal where he allegedly paid US$18.5 million in bribes for a permit to mine titanium in India, something Firtash denies.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<http://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-firtash-extradition-granted-austria-u-s/28322886.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-21-6-4"></a>

Context: Israeli–Palestinian conflict, Hebron shooting incident.

**Archived source account.** Following last month's manslaughter conviction, Israeli soldier Elor Azaria is sentenced to 18 months in prison by a military court for, during a violent incident, his deadly shooting of the wounded, unarmed, prone Palestinian Abdel Fattah al-Sharif, who had stabbed a soldier last March in Hebron.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS News](<http://www.cbsnews.com/news/elor-azaria-israeli-soldier-sentenced-for-fatal-shooting-of-palestinian-attacker/>).

<a id="event-2017-02-21-6-6"></a>

Context: United States immigration ban.

**Archived source account.** The Trump administration releases a new memo that sets the policy for the deportation of undocumented migrants accused of any crime.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<http://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/trump-enforcement-plan-has-immigrants-bracing-raids-deportations-n723771>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-02-21-7-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Azerbaijani First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva, who is widely considered to be in line to succeed her husband, is named vice president.

Source citations (as archived): [BNO News](<https://web.archive.org/web/20170222110232/http://bnonews.com/news/index.php/news/id5701>).

<a id="event-2017-02-21-7-2"></a>

Context: Nagorno-Karabakh constitutional referendum, 2017.

**Archived source account.** In a referendum held yesterday in the breakaway state of Nagorno-Karabakh (a region long claimed by both Azerbaijan and Armenia), 87.6% of voters approve changing the country's governance system from semi-presidential to full presidential, therefore abolishing the position of prime minister.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<http://www.rferl.org/a/nagorno-karabakh-referendum-azerbaijan-armenia/28323000.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-21-7-4"></a>

Context: Ecuadorian general election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** A runoff presidential election, between former vice-president Lenín Moreno and former bank president Guillermo Lasso, is scheduled for Sunday, April 2 since no candidate gained at least 40 percent of the vote in Sunday's poll. With 95.3 percent of votes counted, Moreno received 39.21 percent of valid votes and Lasso had 28.34 percent.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ecuador-election-idUSKBN1601UN>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2017-02-21-8-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Several new species of tiny frogs are discovered in India.

Source citations (as archived): [CBS News](<http://www.cbsnews.com/news/tiny-new-frog-species-found-in-india/>).

### 2017-02-22

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1360645631](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20February%2022&oldid=1360645631>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-02-22-0-1"></a>

Context: Syrian Civil War, Raqqa offensive.

**Archived source account.** U.S.-backed SDF forces on two fronts meet up northeast of Raqqa, encircling a pocket of villages still held by ISIS.

Source citations (as archived): [Rudaw](<http://www.rudaw.net/english/middleeast/syria/220220171>).

<a id="event-2017-02-22-0-3"></a>

Context: Yemeni Civil War (2015–present).

**Archived source account.** A Houthi missile attack on a Yemeni military camp near the port city of Mocha kills Major General Ahmed Saif al-Yafei, Yemen's deputy chief of staff, and several others.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-idUSKBN1610ND?il=0>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2017-02-22-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Six people are killed after a fire broke out in a factory in Attapur, Hyderabad, India.

Source citations (as archived): [The Hindu](<https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/six-people-including-four-workers-died-in-a-fire-accident/article17345908.ece>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2017-02-22-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Amnesty International releases a report criticizing the rise of populist leaders such as Donald Trump of the United States, Viktor Orbán of Hungary, Rodrigo Duterte of the Philippines and Recep Tayyip Erdoğan of Turkey.

Source citations (as archived): [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2017/02/22/amnesty-international-just-went-there-new-report-compares-politics-today-to-the-1930s/>).

<a id="event-2017-02-22-2-2"></a>

Context: Headscarf controversy in Turkey.

**Archived source account.** The Turkish government lifts the ban prohibiting female army officers from wearing a Hijab. The military is the last Turkish institution to end the ban.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-39053064>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-02-22-3-1"></a>

Context: 2017 Mexico–United States diplomatic crisis.

**Archived source account.** Mexican Foreign Minister Luis Videgaray Caso rejects and condemns the United States's new plan on deporting undocumented immigrants, stating that Mexico cannot "accept unilateral decisions imposed by one government on another."

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-39054999>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-02-22-4-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** South Africa's North Gauteng High Court rules the government's decision last October to withdraw from the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court was unconstitutional, and instructs the government to revoke its notice of withdrawal.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<http://bigstory.ap.org/article/109805faac52454283bc57d8fa7006d3/south-african-court-rules-against-icc-withdrawal>); [NPR](<https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2017/02/22/516620190/court-blocks-south-africas-withdrawal-from-international-criminal-court>).

<a id="event-2017-02-22-4-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Former Chief Executive of Hong Kong Donald Tsang is sentenced to 20 months in prison for corruption, becoming the highest officeholder in Hong Kong's history to be convicted.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-39048543>).

<a id="event-2017-02-22-4-3"></a>

Context: 2017 Olathe, Kansas shooting.

**Archived source account.** In an apparent hate crime, an Indian engineer is shot dead and another injured in Olathe, Kansas.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/24/world/asia/kansas-attack-possible-hate-crime-srinivas-kuchibhotla.html>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-02-22-5-1"></a>

Context: Transgender rights in the United States.

**Archived source account.** The Trump administration revokes Obama-era orders on protection of gender identity under Title IX.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-39047883>); [CNN](<http://www.cnn.com/2017/02/22/politics/doj-withdraws-federal-protections-on-transgender-bathrooms-in-school>).

<a id="event-2017-02-22-5-3"></a>

Context: French presidential election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** François Bayrou drops out in an effort to boost Emmanuel Macron.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/22/french-elections-centrist-bayrou-offers-alliance-with-macron>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2017-02-22-6-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** NASA and the European Southern Observatory announce the discovery of four new Earth-like planets in the Goldilocks zone of the star TRAPPIST-1, in addition to the three discovered there last year.

Source citations (as archived): [The Atlantic](<https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2017/02/seven-exoplanets/517446/>); [NBC News](<http://www.nbcnews.com/mach/space/watch-live-nasa-announces-major-exoplanet-discovery-n724111>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2017-02-22-7-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Eastern Sports Club's manager Chan Yuen-ting becomes the first woman to coach a male football club in a top-flight continental competition with managing team against Guangzhou Evergrande in the AFC Champions League.

Source citations (as archived): [Sky Sports](<http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11996/10777580/chan-yuen-ting-becomes-first-woman-to-manage-in-mens-continental-top-flight-competition>).

<a id="event-2017-02-22-7-2"></a>

Context: 2024 Summer Olympics.

**Archived source account.** Budapest withdraws its bid, leaving Paris and Los Angeles as the two candidate cities for hosting the 2024 competition.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-olympics-2024-budapest-idUSKBN1610YO>).

Context: French presidential election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** The Alaska Aces ice hockey team announce that the 2016–17 ECHL season will be the team's last after 28 seasons of play, following a downturn in the Alaskan economy and sagging ticket sales. \{\{Dead link\|date=May 2020 \|bot=InternetArchiveBot \|fix-attempted=yes \}\}

### 2017-02-24

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-02-24-0-1"></a>

Context: Syrian Civil War, Battle of al-Bab.

Context: Yemeni Civil War (2015–present).

<a id="event-2017-02-24-2-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Israel denies entry to Omar Shakir, a researcher for Human Rights Watch and an American citizen, because the organization engages in so-called Palestinian propaganda. Context: Presidency of Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** The Trump administration signals that it plans a crackdown on U.S states that legalize the use of cannabis.

Source citations (as archived): [Los Angeles Times](<http://www.latimes.com/politics/la-na-pol-trump-marijuana-20170223-story.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-24-3-4"></a>

Context: Presidency of Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** The Justice Department plans to expand the use of private prisons.

Source citations (as archived): [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/pwa/#https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/national-security/justice-department-will-again-use-private-prisons/2017/02/23/da395d02-fa0e-11e6-be05-1a3817ac21a5_story.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-24-3-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Protesters in South Africa rally against immigration.

Source citations (as archived): [France 24](<http://www.france24.com/en/20170224-south-africa-anti-immigrant-protesters-clash-nigerian>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-02-24-4-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Philippine vice president Leni Robredo defends her fellow Liberal party-mate Leila de Lima who was arrested for alleged drug trafficking. Robredo calls de Lima's arrest political harassment.

Source citations (as archived): [PDI](<http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/874974/robredo-calls-de-limas-arrest-political-harassment>).

<a id="event-2017-02-24-4-2"></a>

Context: Presidency of Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** The Trump White House bars The New York Times, CNN, the Los Angeles Times, the New York Daily News, The Hill, the Daily Mail, BBC, Politico, and BuzzFeed from a Friday press "gaggle." Generally conservative, mostly new, outlets were permitted entry, such as Breitbart News, One America News Network, and The Washington Times. Also allowed in were ABC News, CBS News, NBC News, The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg News, and Fox News. Time magazine and the Associated Press could have attended but chose not to in protest. The White House Correspondents’ Association, which represents the press corps, quickly rebuked the White House’s actions. \{\{Dead link\|date=August 2019 \|bot=InternetArchiveBot \|fix-attempted=yes \}\}

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<http://bigstory.ap.org/article/9d04bb7ccf60468987c582b4ee9c7e24/white-house-bars-major-news-outlets-media-gaggle>); [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-media-idUSKBN1632JG?il=0>); [NBC News](<http://www.nbcnews.com/politics/white-house/white-house-excludes-several-outlets-press-gaggle-n725366>); [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/24/us/politics/white-house-sean-spicer-briefing.html?_r=0>); [The Hill](<http://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/media-slams-limited-wh-press-access/ar-AAnksZB?ocid=edgsp>).

### 2017-02-25

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1256030720](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20February%2025&oldid=1256030720>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-02-25-0-1"></a>

Context: Syrian Civil War.

**Archived source account.** The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports that militants attacked two Syrian Armed Forces bases in Homs, killing at least 42 people, including a senior intelligence officer.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<http://www.jpost.com/Breaking-News/Attack-on-Syrian-security-forces-in-Homs-kills-14-482546>); [SBS](<http://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/2017/02/25/suicide-attacks-bases-syrias-homs-kill-42-monitor>).

<a id="event-2017-02-25-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021).

**Archived source account.** According to officials, at least 11 people, mostly police officers, are killed outside a mosque in Jowzjan Province in an ambush by militants. The Taliban claimed responsibility for the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<http://www.rferl.org/a/ten-afghan-police-officers-killed/28331939.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-25-0-5"></a>

Context: Iraqi Civil War (2014–2017).

**Archived source account.** Shifa Gardi, a prominent female reporter for Rudaw Media Network, is killed by a roadside bomb while reporting on the battle for Mosul.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-39089148>).

<a id="event-2017-02-25-0-7"></a>

Context: Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.

**Archived source account.** Clashes erupt between Nagorno-Karabakh separatists and Azerbaijani forces in the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh region. The Azerbaijan Ministry of Defense confirmed casualties on its side while the separatist forces claim to have no casualties. Both sides blame each other for the flareup in fighting.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<http://www.rferl.org/a/armenians-azerbaijanis-trade-accusations-over-karabakh-fighting/28331782.html>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-02-25-1-1"></a>

Context: France–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** French President François Hollande reproaches U.S. President Donald Trump for his disparaging comments about Paris at Friday's Conservative Political Action Conference, noting that allies should have more respect and support for each other.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-usa-paris-idUSKBN1640CD>); [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/25/world/europe/frances-president-criticizes-trump-over-paris-remarks.html?_r=0>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-02-25-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** German police shoot a man, who was trying to escape after apparently driving into a group of pedestrians in a central square in Heidelberg. A 73-year-old man was killed and two other people injured. Police do not believe terrorism is involved.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-39091858>); [Deutsche Welle](<http://www.dw.com/en/heidelberg-pedestrians-rammed-by-car-police-shoot-attacker/a-37717837>); [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-germany-attack-idUSKBN1640NW>).

<a id="event-2017-02-25-2-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** A suspected drunken driver plows his car into a crowd watching the Krewe of Endymion parade at the New Orleans Mardi Gras. Dozens are injured, with 28 people, including a child and a police officer, taken to seven hospitals, five in critical condition.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<https://web.archive.org/web/20170228145549/http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/stories/U/US_MARDI_GRAS_CAR_HITS_CROWD?SITE=AP&amp;SECTION=HOME&amp;TEMPLATE=DEFAULT&amp;CTIME=2017-02-25-21-12-09>); [New Orleans Times-Picayune](<http://www.nola.com/traffic/index.ssf/2017/02/12_hurt_when_vehicle_plows_int.html#incart_big-photo>); [AP](<http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-02-26/new-orleans:-dozens-injured-after-vehicle-hits-crowd/8304624>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-02-25-3-1"></a>

Context: An act to repeal the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act.

**Archived source account.** A leaked memo from House Republicans reveals cutting provisions from Obamacare such as Medicaid expansions and subsidies for health insurance.

Source citations (as archived): [CNBC](<https://www.cnbc.com/2017/02/24/gop-draft-health-care-bill-cuts-medicaid-insurance-subsidies.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-25-3-3"></a>

Context: Democratic National Committee chairmanship election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** Voting takes place in Atlanta, Georgia, to elect a new Chair of the Democratic National Committee. Candidates include Sally Boynton Brown, Keith Ellison, Jehmu Greene and former United States Secretary of Labor Tom Perez.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://edition.cnn.com/2017/02/25/politics/dnc-chair-election/>).

<a id="event-2017-02-25-3-4"></a>

Context: Democratic National Committee chairmanship election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** In a second round of voting, Tom Perez is elected Chair of the DNC with 235 votes. Perez names Congressman Keith Ellison Deputy Party Chair.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<http://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/dnc-race-tom-perez-becomes-dnc-chair-narrow-election-victory-n725596>); [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/powerpost/tom-perez-elected-as-first-latino-leader-of-democratic-party/2017/02/25/1fd76f52-fad7-11e6-9845-576c69081518_story.html>).

<a id="event-2017-02-25-3-6"></a>

Context: Presidency of Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** Donald Trump announces he will not attend the 2017 White House Correspondents' Dinner, following recent friction between his administration and various news organizations.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-39093434>).

### 2017-02-27

<a id="event-2017-02-27-2-0"></a>

### 2017-02-28

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1256030738](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20February%2028&oldid=1256030738>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-02-28-0-1"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021).

**Archived source account.** Twelve Afghan National Police officers are killed in a Taliban "infiltration attack" in the southern Helmand Province.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-39112831>).

<a id="event-2017-02-28-0-3"></a>

Context: Gaza–Israel conflict.

#### Business and economics

<a id="event-2017-02-28-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Hershey Company announces it will cut about 15 percent of its global workforce (~2,700 jobs) to return its international businesses to profitability as quickly as possible. The layoffs will have a greater impact on the international workforce.

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2017-02-28-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A small plane crashes in a residential area of Riverside, California, killing at least three people, all of whom were passengers on the plane. No one on the ground was injured.

<a id="event-2017-02-28-2-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** A police sniper accidentally fires his weapon while changing position and injures two people during a speech by French President François Hollande in Villognon.

<a id="event-2017-02-28-2-2"></a>

Context: 2016–17 Turkish purges.

**Archived source account.** About 330 people with alleged links to last year's coup attempt stand trial at a prison outside Ankara on charges of murder and attempting to overthrow the government, the largest trial to date.

<a id="event-2017-02-28-3-3"></a>

Israeli police are evacuating nine homes in the settlement, despite hunger strikes and people barricading themselves inside.

## March

### 2017-03-01

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1087126420](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20March%201&oldid=1087126420>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-03-01-0-1"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021).

**Archived source account.** At least 16 people were killed and 40 more wounded after two suicide bombers attacked Kabul. The Taliban claimed responsibility for the attacks.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<http://www.rferl.org/a/afghanistan-kabul-blast-gunbattle/28340312.html>).

#### Business and economics

<a id="event-2017-03-01-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Dow Jones Industrial Average rises above 21,000 points, reaching an all-time high.

Source citations (as archived): [Los Angeles Times](<http://www.latimes.com/business/la-fi-markets-20170301-story.html>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-03-01-2-1"></a>

Context: Georgia–European Union relations.

**Archived source account.** The European Union formally grants Georgian citizens visa-free travel to its member states, with the exception of Ireland and the United Kingdom. The signed documents will be published on March 8, and officially enter into force on March 28.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<http://www.rferl.org/a/georgia-eu-visa-free-documents-signing/28340527.html>).

<a id="event-2017-03-01-2-3"></a>

Context: Syrian Civil War.

**Archived source account.** Russia and China veto a draft United Nations Security Council resolution sponsored by France, the United Kingdom and the United States calling for sanctions against the Syrian government and President Bashar al-Assad over allegations that the government used chemical weapons in the conflict.

Source citations (as archived): [RT](<https://www.rt.com/news/378930-russia-china-un-veto-syria/>); [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/mar/01/russia-and-china-veto-un-resolution-to-impose-sanctions-on-syria>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-03-01-3-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** An avalanche kills four skiers in Tyrol, Austria.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-39283797>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-03-15-2-1"></a>

Context: Dutch general election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** Voters in the Netherlands go to the polls for a general election. Exit polls suggest that incumbent Prime Minister Mark Rutte's People's Party for Freedom and Democracy will win the most seats in the election.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-39275194>).

<a id="event-2017-03-15-2-3"></a>

Context: United States immigration ban.

**Archived source account.** A U.S. federal judge in Hawaii, finding the revised federal immigration/refugee executive order violates the U.S. Constitution's religious establishment clause, grants the state of Hawaii's motion for a nationwide temporary restraining order on these rules that were set to become effective at midnight. President Donald Trump vows to appeal this ruling. Two other federal courts held hearings on similar requests filed by the states of Maryland and Washington; neither of these judges issued a ruling.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-immigration-court-idUSKBN16M17N>); [Honolulu Star-Advertiser](<http://www.staradvertiser.com/2017/03/15/breaking-news/hawaii-in-federal-court-to-challenge-trumps-travel-ban/>).

### 2017-03-17

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1089954466](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20March%2017&oldid=1089954466>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-03-17-0-1"></a>

Context: March 2017 Israel–Syria incident, Israeli–Syrian ceasefire line incidents during the Syrian Civil War.

**Archived source account.** The Israeli Air Force launches several airstrikes on targets inside Syria, and for the first time, publicly claims responsibility. Syrian air defenses responded by launching missiles at the aircraft, and thereupon Israeli Arrow 3 missiles were launched in response to the counter-offensive. Israel stated that it was targeting suspected weapons shipments to Hezbollah in Lebanon, adding that the Israeli military will keep intervening until they believe such shipments have ceased. According to the Syrian Army, four Israeli jets entered its airspace and struck targets near Palmyra.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://www.cnn.com/2017/03/17/middleeast/israel-jets-syria-strikes/index.html>); [AP](<http://bigstory.ap.org/article/b0005340c957486e88144994668c34d8/syrian-missiles-fired-israeli-jets-struck-syria>).

<a id="event-2017-03-17-0-3"></a>

Context: Yemeni Civil War (2015-present).

**Archived source account.** An unknown perpetrator using an Apache helicopter fires upon a boat carrying Somali refugees off the coast of Yemen, killing at least 40 of them, injuring 35 more.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-refugees-idUSKBN16O0UI>); [AFP](<https://web.archive.org/web/20170320000658/http://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/33-somali-refugees-shot-dead-on-red-sea-yemen-officials/ar-BByfsNR>).

<a id="event-2017-03-17-0-5"></a>

Context: War in North-West Pakistan.

**Archived source account.** Gunmen raid a Pakistani military post near the border with Afghanistan, killing at least eight people. Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, a faction of Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan, claim responsibility.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/03/clashes-pakistan-afghanistan-border-kill-170317061451793.html>).

<a id="event-2017-03-17-0-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** In Spain, the Basque separatist group ETA announces that it will fully disarm by April 8, 2017.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-39305685>).

### 2017-03-18

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-03-18-0-1"></a>

Context: Syrian Civil War.

**Archived source account.** Around 1,500–2,000 people leave al-Waer district of Homs today for their preferred destination of either Northern Homs Governorate, Idlib Governorate or Turkish Army positions in Northern Aleppo Governorate. Up to 15,000 to 20,000 people including armed militants, their families and supporters will leave the besieged district in the coming weeks with the rest of the population reconciling and receiving aid.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-39315389>); [Al Masdar News](<https://www.almasdarnews.com/article/first-batch-rebels-leaves-last-stronghold-syrias-homs-photos/>).

<a id="event-2017-03-18-0-3"></a>

Context: Battle of Mosul.

**Archived source account.** Thousands of Iraqis flee western Mosul as the battle between Iraqi and allied forces and ISIL militants escalates in the densely populated Old City.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-iraq-mosul-idUSKBN16P0NA>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2017-03-18-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Chuck Berry, pioneering rock music singer and guitarist, dies in the U.S. state of Missouri at the age of 90. Berry was one of the first inductees in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-39318602>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-03-18-2-1"></a>

Context: Estonia–United Kingdom relations.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2017/mar/18/british-troops-land-in-estonia-for-nato-mission-to-deter-russia>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-03-18-3-1"></a>

Context: March 2017 Île-de-France attacks.

**Archived source account.** French security forces shoot suspect Ziyed Ben Belgacem dead in Paris' Orly Airport after he put the pellet gun to her head and took away an assault rifle from one of three soldiers from "Sentinelle" operation patrolling the airport. Belgacem had earlier shot a police officer with a pellet gun. Later, he had threatened a bar and then carjacked another vehicle to the airport.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-39314250#>).

### 2017-03-21

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1089955072](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20March%2021&oldid=1089955072>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-03-21-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Citing security concerns because of recent terrorist activity, the American and British governments impose a ban affecting inbound-passengers flying from much of the Middle East and North Africa. The ban includes airplane cabin passenger-accessible items such as laptops, tablets, and other electronic devices which are larger than a smartphone. Larger such electronic devices will still be allowed on board in checked baggage which is thus more closely screened and passenger-inaccessible.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://money.cnn.com/2017/03/21/news/airline-electronics-ban-middle-east-africa/index.html?iid=hp-toplead-intl>); [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-39333424>).

<a id="event-2017-03-21-0-2"></a>

Context: War in Somalia.

**Archived source account.** A car bomb explodes at a checkpoint near the Villa Somalia, the President of Somalia Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed's official residence in Mogadishu, killing at least five people.

Source citations (as archived): [The Citizen](<http://citizen.co.za/news/news-africa/1463969/powerful-explosion-rocks-mogadishu-say-police/>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-03-21-1-1"></a>

Context: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

**Archived source account.** Tasnim News Agency reports that, in a Nowruz speech, Supreme Leader of Iran Ali Khamenei said experts in his country can enrich uranium to 99 percent. ISNA reports that Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif is threatening to quit the Iran nuclear deal if the United States blocks Iran's version of the deal's implementation.

Source citations (as archived): [Kleine Zeitung](<http://www.kleinezeitung.at/service/newsticker/5187457/Iran-droht-den-USA-mit-Ausstieg-aus-dem-Atomabkommen>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-03-21-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** In a 6–2 decision (NLRB v. SW General, Inc), the U.S. Supreme Court puts new restrictions on presidential powers, limiting a president's authority to staff certain top government posts in a case involving an appointment to the National Labor Relations Board saying that under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act, a person cannot serve as the acting head of a federal agency once the president nominates him or her to permanently serve in the role if it is a position that requires U.S. Senate confirmation. The court upholds a lower court's ruling that then-President Barack Obama exceeded his legal authority with his temporary appointment of an NLRB general counsel in 2011. The ruling will give President Donald Trump and future presidents less flexibility in filling jobs that require Senate confirmation.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-court-executive-idUSKBN16S25E>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-03-21-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Bruno Le Roux resigns as France's Minister of the Interior amid a jobs scandal involving two of his daughters. Using public funds, Bruno had hired his 15 and 16-year-old daughters as parliamentary assistants while he was serving as a deputy in the French National Assembly.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-39346617>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2017-03-21-4-1"></a>

Context: In International professional baseball.

**Archived source account.** The United States defeats Japan 2–1 at Dodger Stadium to advance to the 2017 World Baseball Classic's final. This is the first time that the U.S. has done so in the tournament's 11-year history.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/mlb/2017/03/22/usa-beats-japan-reaches-world-baseball-classic-final-first-time/99480456/>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-03-22-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Former Congolese Vice President and warlord Jean-Pierre Bemba, sentenced last year by the International Criminal Court (ICC) to 18 years in prison for war crimes, is given an additional 12 months and fined 300,000 euros for bribing witnesses during an earlier ICC trial. The court also handed jail terms and fines for alleged interference in his trial to members of his legal team.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/mar/22/jean-pierre-bemba-jailed-bribing-witnesses-congolese-war-crimes>).

<a id="event-2017-03-22-3-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** A series of shootings in Rothschild, Wisconsin, leave at least four people dead, including a police officer.

<a id="event-2017-03-22-3-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** A jury acquits the former head of the now-closed Massachusetts pharmacy, New England Compounding Center, Barry Cadden, on 25 counts of second-degree murder but convicts him of racketeering and other crimes in a meningitis outbreak that was traced to fungus-contaminated drugs and killed 64 people across the country. Cadden disregarded sanitary conditions to boost production and make more money.

Source citations (as archived): [Boston.com](<https://www.boston.com/news/local-news/2017/03/22/verdict-reached-in-trial-over-deadly-us-meningitis-outbreak>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2017-03-22-4-1"></a>

Context: 2017 World Baseball Classic.

**Archived source account.** In the final, the United States defeats Puerto Rico 8–0 to claim its first title in the event. Toronto Blue Jays starting pitcher Marcus Stroman, who threw six hitless innings in the final for Team USA, is named tournament MVP.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<http://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/18981558/team-usa-routs-puerto-rico-win-first-world-baseball-classic>).

### 2017-03-23

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1242330060](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20March%2023&oldid=1242330060>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-03-23-1-1"></a>

Context: 2017 Westminster attack.

**Archived source account.** Authorities arrest at least eight people in connection with yesterday's attack.

Source citations (as archived): [Fox News](<http://www.foxnews.com/world/2017/03/23/london-attack-british-police-reportedly-make-arrests-in-raid-on-home.html>).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-1-2"></a>

Context: 2017 Westminster attack.

**Archived source account.** London's Metropolitan Police Service announces that the attacker is British-born Khalid Masood, previously questioned by British authorities for connections to terrorism.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-security-attacker-idUSKBN16U26E>).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-1-3"></a>

Context: 2017 Westminster attack.

**Archived source account.** The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant claims responsibility.

Source citations (as archived): [The Telegraph](<https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2017/03/23/london-attack-seven-arrested-police-raid-properties-linked-islamist/>).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-1-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** A former Ukrainian soldier assassinates former Russian Duma deputy Denis Voronenkov in the Ukrainian capital Kiev. In December 2016, he received Ukrainian citizenship. Ilya Ponomarev says Voronenkov was heading to a meeting with him.

Source citations (as archived): [The Moscow Times](<https://themoscowtimes.com/news/breaking-former-russian-parliamentarian-and-putin-critic-shot-dead-in-kiev-57513>).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-1-6"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021).

**Archived source account.** Taliban insurgents seize control of the strategic town of Sangin in the southern Helmand Province after a year-long battle with Afghan security forces.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-39365330>).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-1-8"></a>

Context: 2017 Antwerp attack.

**Archived source account.** A man drives into a crowd of pedestrians in Antwerp, Belgium, injuring several people. Police arrest the man, who is believed to be North African born and living in France.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/03/23/world/europe/antwerp-belgium-car-attack.html?_r=0>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2017-03-23-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The American city of Fort Collins, Colorado, announces its intention to appeal a federal judge's ruling that blocked the city’s ban on women appearing topless in public.

Source citations (as archived): [USA Today](<https://web.archive.org/web/20170325202317/http://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/city-vows-to-appeal-ruling-that-allows-women-to-go-topless/ar-BByBZSi?li=BBnbfcL&amp;ocid=iehp>).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-2-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Cardinal William Henry Keeler, who was Archbishop of Baltimore from 1989 to 2007, dies at the age of 86. At the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB), he served as the moderator for Catholic-Jewish relations as well as the Chair for the Bishops’ Committee for Ecumenical and Interreligious Affairs between 1984 and 1987.

Source citations (as archived): [Catholic News Agency](<https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/baltimore-mourns-cardinal-keeler-former-archbishop-81157>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2017-03-23-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A series of explosions on a military base near the Ukrainian city of Balakliya forces thousands to be evacuated from their homes.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-39363416>).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-3-2"></a>

Context: Sinking of MV Sewol.

**Archived source account.** The South Korean government raises the wreckage of the MV Sewol from the sea near the South Korean island of Donggeochado. The ferry sank in April 2014, killing 304 people.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-39361944>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-03-23-4-1"></a>

Context: American Health Care Act of 2017.

**Archived source account.** The United States House of Representatives approaches a vote on a replacement plan for the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (aka Obamacare).

<a id="event-2017-03-23-4-2"></a>

Context: American Health Care Act of 2017.

**Archived source account.** The U.S. House postpones the vote due to a lack of support and slow progress in dealmaking.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://www.cnn.com/2017/03/23/politics/house-health-care-vote/>).

#### Science and environment

<a id="event-2017-03-23-5-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The night parrot is confirmed sighted (and photographed) in Western Australia for first time in nearly 100 years.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2017/mar/23/night-parrot-sighting-confirmed-in-western-australia-for-first-time-in-100-years>).

### 2017-03-24

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-03-24-0-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Six Chechen soldiers, along with six militants, are killed in a nighttime attack on a Russian National Guard base in Chechnya.

<a id="event-2017-03-24-0-3"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan (2001–present).

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-39383726>).

<a id="event-2017-03-24-0-4"></a>

<a id="event-2017-03-24-0-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** On Friday night a man begins to shoot in a Lille Metro station in Lille, France. Three people are injured, including being shot in the leg and neck. The gunman is not thought to be a terrorist, and is still on the run.

<a id="event-2017-03-24-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Proactiva notes the finding of five corpses the Libyan coast; these were floating near two capsized boats which could each hold more than 100 people.

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-03-24-2-1"></a>

Context: France–Russia relations.

**Archived source account.** French National Front presidential candidate Marine Le Pen meets with Russian president Vladimir Putin and afterwards urges that European Union sanctions on Russia be lifted.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-39375969>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-03-24-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak is released from detention in Cairo.

<a id="event-2017-03-24-3-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Gambia's justice minister Abubacarr Tambadou states that the country will establish a Truth and Reconciliation Commission "within the next six months" to investigate allegations of abuse dating from the time of former President Yahya Jammeh. According to Tambadou, public hearings are scheduled to get underway by year's end.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-39378345>).

<a id="event-2017-03-24-3-2"></a>

<a id="event-2017-03-24-4-2"></a>

Context: 2017 Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act replacement proposals.

**Archived source account.** The replacement plan for the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (aka Obamacare) is withdrawn after Republican leaders fail to gain enough support. The failure of the Trump administration to repeal the act means it will remain law in the United States.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-39387550>).

<a id="event-2017-03-24-4-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Gilmar Pisas is sworn in as Prime Minister of Curaçao.

<a id="event-2017-03-24-5-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** NASA astronaut Shane Kimbrough and ESA astronaut Thomas Pesquet take a spacewalk outside of the International Space Station to prepare the vessel for new arrivals.

Source citations (as archived): [Space.com](<http://www.space.com/36198-space-station-astronauts-march-24-spacewalk-webcast.html>).

In the Midwest Region in Kansas City, Missouri, Oregon defeats Kansas 74–60, giving the Ducks their first Final Four appearance since winning the first NCAA Tournament in 1939.

<a id="event-2017-03-27-4-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The National Football League (NFL) owners approve, by a 31–1 vote, the move of the Oakland Raiders to Las Vegas, Nevada, for the 2019 or 2020 season. The Las Vegas Raiders will become the second top-level professional sports franchise in the city, following the National Hockey League's Vegas Golden Knights, which will begin play in October 2017. The move now awaits completion of a new Raiders stadium, until which time the Raiders will continue playing home games in Oakland. Bank of America has issued the Raiders $650 million in credit to purchase land and build the new stadium in Clark County.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC Sports](<http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/03/27/raiders-vote-coming-soon/>); [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2017/03/27/nfl-approves-raiders-move-to-las-vegas/?pushid=58d9563104329f1d0000000b&amp;tid=notifi_push_breaking-news>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2017-03-28-6-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Accounts of sightings of animals thought to resemble the extinct thylacine, the largest known carnivorous marsupial of modern times, prompt a search in the Far North of the Australian state of Queensland.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2017/mar/28/tasmanian-tiger-sighting-search-thylacine-queensland-australia>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2017-03-28-7-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** In association football, and as CONMEBOL qualification for the 2018 FIFA World Cup continues, the Argentina forward Lionel Messi is banned for four matches, five and a half hours before kickoff in his team's match against Bolivia.

<a id="event-2017-03-29-4-1"></a>

Context: United States immigration ban.

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

Context: Cyclone Debbie.

<a id="event-2017-03-30-1-5"></a>

Context: Interstate 85 bridge collapse.

**Archived source account.** A fire results in the collapse of a bridge on Interstate 85 in Atlanta, Georgia, during rush hour, stranding motorists and resulting in a state of emergency. Atlanta mayor Kasim Reed calls the situation a "transportation crisis" that could close the affected stretch of highway for days or weeks. A 2015 report stated that the highway carried nearly a quarter-million vehicles a day.

Source citations (as archived): [NBC News](<http://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/bridge-collapses-atlanta-freeway-fire-during-rush-hour-n740871>).

<a id="event-2017-03-30-2-1"></a>

This appears as a policy shift, since under president Barack Obama’s administration, the United States made the departure of Assad a key policy aim.

Opposition leaders call it a "coup", while Peru recalls its ambassador.

<a id="event-2017-03-30-4-5"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://www.cnn.com/2017/03/30/politics/senate-intelligence-committee-hearing-russia/>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2017-03-30-5-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Scientific Reports publishes Carthage College research that Daspletosaurus horneri, from the same Tyrannosauridae family as the Tyrannosaurus rex, had a sensitive nose. The research describes that foramina sprouted from the trigeminal nerve at the snout and jaws possibly enabling the behavioral functions of exploration, courtship, nesting, foreplay, and parental investment.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/science/2017/mar/30/tyrannosaurus-rex-was-a-sensitive-lover-new-dinosaur-discovery-suggests>).

<a id="event-2017-03-30-5-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** SpaceX successfully places the SES-10 telecommunications satellite on a geostationary transfer orbit. The event is notable because of the implied economic cost savings of reusing, for the first time, a used Falcon 9 first stage which had previously been recovered. That first stage had previously launched a Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station and landed on an autonomous drone ship during the CRS-8 mission.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/03/30/science/spacex-launches-a-satellite-with-a-partly-used-rocket.html>).

**Archived source account.** An attack occurs at a Sufi shrine near Sargodha, Pakistan, killing more than 20 people. Authorities arrest a main suspect and several others.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-39471017>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-04-02-3-1"></a>

Context: Armenian parliamentary election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** Voters in Armenia go to the polls for an election, the first since constitutional changes were approved in a referendum in 2015, which changed the country's governance from a semi-presidential system to a parliamentary republic. Opinion polls predict a tight race between the nationalist Republican Party, led by President Serzh Sargsyan, and the centre-right Prosperous Armenia, led by Gagik Tsarukyan. With votes from 64% of the polling stations counted, the Republican Party leads with 49.7% of votes.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<https://www.rferl.org/a/armenian-vote-parliament-sarkisian-tsarukian/28404992.html>); [TASS](<http://tass.com/world/938878>).

<a id="event-2017-04-02-3-3"></a>

Context: Serbian presidential election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** Voters in Serbia go to the polls for an election, which Prime Minister Aleksandar Vučić of the conservative Serbian Progressive Party is expected to win. In projections, Vučić gets around 55% of the votes, avoiding a second round.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<https://www.rferl.org/a/vucic-serbia-presidential-election/28404991.html>); [CNBC](<https://www.cnbc.com/2017/04/03/serbias-aleksandar-vucic-confirms-domination-with-presidential-win.html>).

<a id="event-2017-04-02-3-5"></a>

Context: Ecuadorian general election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** Voters in Ecuador return to the polls for the second round of a presidential election, which Lenín Moreno of the socialist PAIS Alliance is predicted to narrowly win over the center-right Creating Opportunities's Guillermo Lasso. With 94.18% of the votes counted, Moreno leads with 51.07%. According to the national election commission, it was a transparent and successful election.

Source citations (as archived): [SBS News](<http://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/2017/04/02/ecuador-determines-its-future-key-poll-and-maybe-assanges>); [TeleSUR](<http://www.telesurtv.net/english/news/Ecuadors-Lenin-Moreno-Defeats-Banker-in-Presidential-Election-20170402-0037.html>).

#### Sports

<a id="event-2017-04-02-4-1"></a>

Context: 2017 NCAA Division I Women's Basketball Championship Game.

**Archived source account.** South Carolina defeats fellow Southeastern Conference team Mississippi State 67–55 for the Gamecocks' first national title.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<http://www.espn.com/ncw/recap?gameId=400949226>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-04-03-3-1"></a>

Context: LGBT rights in Russia.

**Archived source account.** Russian authorities arrest more than 100 gay men in Chechnya, including television personalities and religious figures, for "nontraditional sexual orientation." The Novaya Gazeta newspaper reported that three of the arrested men have been killed, while others reportedly were released for family honor killing. Chechen Republic leader Ramzan Kadyrov's spokesperson said this report contains “absolute lies and disinformation” since there are no homosexuals in Chechnya.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/apr/02/chechen-police-rounded-up-100-gay-men-report-russian-newspaper-chechnya>); [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/04/01/world/europe/chechen-authorities-arresting-and-killing-gay-men-russian-paper-says.html>).

<a id="event-2017-04-03-3-3"></a>

Context: Trump Tower wiretapping allegations.

**Archived source account.** Media reports indicate that former National Security Advisor Susan Rice improperly requested the unmasking of some American names, including those of Donald Trump's campaign staff, that had been incidentally collected during national security investigations. A National Security Adviser may request unmasking if specific criteria are met. A Rice associate denies that the unmasking was improper.

Source citations (as archived): [Fox News](<http://www.foxnews.com/politics/2017/04/03/susan-rice-requested-to-unmask-names-trump-transition-officials-sources-say.html>); [Business Insider](<http://www.businessinsider.com/susan-rice-trump-unmask-intelligence-wiretap-2017-4>); [The Blaze](<http://www.theblaze.com/news/2017/04/03/susan-rice-statement-denies-improper-unmasking-but-appears-to-confirm-accusation/>).

<a id="event-2017-04-04-3-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Pope Francis expands the Secretariat for Communications and appoints 13 new consultants in addition to the 16 members added on July 13, 2016. The secretariat was established in June 2015.

Source citations (as archived): [America Magazine](<https://www.americamagazine.org/faith/2017/04/12/father-james-martin-appointed-pope-francis-vatican-department-communications>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-04-12-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Ten people are killed in Inabanga, Bohol, in the Philippines' Central Visayas, after the country's National Police and Armed Forces clash with suspected members of Abu Sayyaf.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN Philippines](<http://cnnphilippines.com/news/2017/04/11/Abu-Sayyaf-firefight-Bohol.html>).

<a id="event-2017-04-12-1-2"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021).

**Archived source account.** A suicide bomber kills at least five people and injures ten more near government offices in Kabul. ISIL claims responsibility for the attack.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/04/suicide-bomb-attack-heart-kabul-kills-170412132809450.html>).

#### Business and economics

<a id="event-2017-04-12-2-1"></a>

Context: History of the United States dollar.

**Archived source account.** In an interview, U.S. President Donald Trump says the U.S. dollar is "getting too strong" and wants to keep interest rates low, causing the U.S. Dollar Index to fall.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<http://uk.reuters.com/article/us-global-forex-idUKKBN17C027>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-04-12-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Sheila Abdus-Salaam, an incumbent associate judge of the New York Court of Appeals and the first African-American woman to serve on the Court of Appeals is found dead in the Hudson River.

Source citations (as archived): [NY1 News](<http://www.ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/news/2017/04/12/court-of-appeals-judge-found-dead-in-hudson-river.html>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-04-12-4-1"></a>

Context: Iranian presidential election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** Former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad registers to run in next month's election for a non-consecutive third term, according to state media.

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<https://www.rferl.org/a/ahmadinejad-registers-iranian-president/28425030.html>).

<a id="event-2017-04-12-4-3"></a>

Context: Protests in South Africa.

**Archived source account.** Julius Malema addresses a large, multi-racial crowd in Pretoria before their march on the Union buildings.

Source citations (as archived): [Weekly Xpose South Africa](<https://web.archive.org/web/20170413234807/https://weeklyxpose.co.za/2017/04/12/malema-warned-marchers-behave/>).

### 2017-04-13

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1087125122](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20April%2013&oldid=1087125122>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-04-13-0-1"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021), April 2017 Nangarhar airstrike.

**Archived source account.** The United States Air Force drops the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast in Nangarhar Province, Afghanistan, reportedly on an ISIL complex of tunnels and caves. This is the first use of the weapon on the battlefield.

Source citations (as archived): [Business Insider](<http://www.businessinsider.com/us-moab-mother-of-all-bombs-isis-afghanistan-2017-4>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2017-04-13-1-1"></a>

Context: 2016–17 South Pacific cyclone season.

**Archived source account.** A state of emergency is declared and coastal areas are evacuated in the Coromandel Peninsula as Cyclone Cook sweeps across the North Island of New Zealand.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-39585868>).

<a id="event-2017-04-13-1-3"></a>

Context: European migrant crisis.

**Archived source account.** A boat carrying migrants sinks off the coast of Libya, with 97 people reported missing. 23 others were rescued by the Libyan coast guard.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/04/97-missing-asylum-seeker-boat-sinks-libya-170413161456485.html>).

#### International relations

<a id="event-2017-04-13-2-1"></a>

Context: North Korea and weapons of mass destruction, North Korea–United States relations.

**Archived source account.** U.S.-based monitoring group 38 North says satellite imagery of North Korea's Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site indicates that preparation for a sixth nuclear weapons test is underway.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/apr/13/north-korea-preparing-for-nuclear-test-satellite-images-suggest>).

<a id="event-2017-04-13-2-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Democratic Republic of the Congo suspends its military cooperation with Belgium.

Source citations (as archived): [Jeune Afrique](<http://www.jeuneafrique.com/429783/politique/rdc-suspend-cooperation-militaire-belgique/>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-04-13-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The European Court of Human Rights rules that Russia had failed to protect students and teachers during the 2004 Beslan school siege, which left 334 people dead, and orders the Russian Government to pay 2,955,000 euros to 409 relatives of the victims. The ruling was quickly denounced by Russia as "unacceptable".

Source citations (as archived): [Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty](<http://www.rferl.org/a/beslan-european-court-rules-russia-failed-to-protect-victims/28427351.html>).

<a id="event-2017-04-13-3-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** One student is murdered and another injured in Mardan, Pakistan over alleged blasphemy. The student who died, Mashal Khan, was known on social media for his secular and liberal views.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-39593302>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-04-13-4-1"></a>

Context: 2017 Venezuelan constitutional crisis.

**Archived source account.** Thousands of people take to the streets in Caracas as Venezuelan authorities acknowledge a fifth death in the protests.

Source citations (as archived): [AP](<http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/stories/L/LT_VENEZUELA_POLITICAL_CRISIS?SITE=AP&amp;SECTION=HOME&amp;TEMPLATE=DEFAULT>).

#### Science and technology

<a id="event-2017-04-13-5-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** NASA announces Saturn's moon Enceladus has the conditions in its global subsurface ocean to support life.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<https://www.theguardian.com/science/2017/apr/13/alien-life-saturn-moon-enceladus-nasa>).

### 2017-04-14

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1276217349](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2017%20April%2014&oldid=1276217349>).

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-04-14-0-1"></a>

Context: War in Afghanistan.

**Archived source account.** The Afghan Ministry of Defense reports as many as 36 suspected ISIL militants were killed while no civilians were harmed in yesterday's bombing in Nangarhar Province using the so-called "mother of all bombs" (GBU-43). The ministry spokesman added these deaths have not been independently verified.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-bomb-idUSKBN17F27U>).

**Archived source account.** A British student is stabbed and killed during an attack on a light-rail train in Jerusalem, Israel. Two other passengers are injured. A Palestinian man with a history of mental problems and other issues is taken into custody by Israeli authorities. Israeli Finance Minister Moshe Kahlon linked the attack to terrorism.

Source citations (as archived): [Haaretz](<http://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/1.783493>).

<a id="event-2017-04-14-0-5"></a>

Context: Somali Civil War (2009–present).

#### Disasters and incidents

<a id="event-2017-04-14-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** A landfill slide in Colombo, Sri Lanka, kills at least 16 people.

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-04-14-2-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Amtrak Police taser a man at New York's Penn Station after the man allegedly became agitated due to a delayed train. Bystanders, falsely believing a shooting had occurred, caused a stampede, injuring more than a dozen people.

Source citations (as archived): [New York Daily News](<http://www.nydailynews.com/new-york/stampeding-mob-flees-penn-station-amtrak-cops-taser-man-article-1.3056434>); [Newsday](<http://www.newsday.com/news/new-york/transit-police-incident-sparks-panic-at-penn-station-1.13469490>).

#### International relations

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://money.cnn.com/2017/04/14/news/north-korea-air-china-pyongyang/>).

<a id="event-2017-04-14-3-3"></a>

Context: European migrant crisis.

**Archived source account.** More than 2,000 migrants are rescued from the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Libya.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-europe-migrants-rescue-idUSKBN17G1HE>).

<a id="event-2017-04-14-3-5"></a>

Context: Global surveillance disclosures (2013–present).

**Archived source account.** The Shadow Brokers group releases files allegedly from the National Security Agency which indicate efforts to monitor financial transactions made through the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-cyber-swift-idUSKBN17G1HC>).

<a id="event-2017-04-14-3-6"></a>

Context: Global surveillance disclosures (2013–present).

**Archived source account.** The release also includes programs targeting Microsoft Windows operating systems. Microsoft announces that it had already fixed most (but not all) of these exploits.

Source citations (as archived): [Engadget](<https://www.engadget.com/2017/04/14/shadow-brokers-dump-windows-zero-day/>); [Motherboard](<https://motherboard.vice.com/en_us/article/we-can-calm-down-microsoft-already-patched-most-of-the-shadow-brokers-exploits>).

<a id="event-2017-04-14-4-1"></a>

Context: Iranian presidential election, 2017.

#### Armed conflicts and attacks

<a id="event-2017-04-15-0-5"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-italy-oldest-idUSKBN17H0JH?il=0>).

#### Disasters and accidents

<a id="event-2017-04-15-2-1"></a>

Context: 2017 Northwest Iran floods.

**Archived source account.** Flash flooding caused by torrential rain leaves at least 17 people dead and 20 others missing in northwestern Iran, according to state television.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/04/flash-floods-kill-17-northwest-iran-170415071058182.html>).

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-04-15-3-1"></a>

Context: Personal and business legal affairs of Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** U.S. President Donald Trump's lawyers tell a federal court, in a case alleging negligence and incitement to riot during a 2016 campaign rally in Louisville, Kentucky, that he is "immune from suit because he is President of the United States." A lawyer for the plaintiffs responds that, in Clinton v. Jones, the Supreme Court found the president could be sued for events that occurred before he took office.

Source citations (as archived): [The Washington Post](<https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/the-fix/wp/2017/04/15/trump-says-he-cant-be-sued-for-violence-at-his-rallies-because-he-won-the-election/>).

#### Politics and elections

<a id="event-2017-04-15-4-2"></a>

Context: Presidency of Donald Trump / Protests against Donald Trump, Tax Day March.

**Archived source account.** Tens of thousands of people march in dozens of U.S. cities and at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort in Palm Beach, Florida, to demand that Trump release his tax returns and to show the public cares about the issue. There were clashes between Trump supporters and protesters at some locations, with 11 people injured and 21 arrested at a riot in Berkeley, California.

Source citations (as archived): [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/04/15/us/politics/tax-day-protests-trump-returns.html?_r=0>); [Reuters](<http://in.reuters.com/article/usa-trump-taxes-idINKBN17I032>); [Los Angeles Times](<http://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-berkeley-trump-rally-20170415-story.html>).

<a id="event-2017-04-15-4-3"></a>

Context: Presidency of Donald Trump.

**Archived source account.** United States Vice President Mike Pence visits Alaska, where he meets with Governor Bill Walker and discusses stationing F-35 squadrons in the state. Pence is beginning a 10-day trip to South Korea, Australia, Indonesia and Japan.

Source citations (as archived): [US News &amp; World Report](<https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/alaska/articles/2017-04-15/pence-meets-with-alaska-governor-ahead-of-asia-trip>).

<a id="event-2017-04-15-4-5"></a>

Context: Iranian presidential election, 2017.

**Archived source account.** Tehran Mayor Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf and First Vice President Eshaq Jahangiri submit their candidacies as registration closes. The final list of approved candidates will be announced on April 27.

Source citations (as archived): [Mehr News](<http://en.mehrnews.com/news/124795/Pre-Guardian-Council-final-list-becomes-exhaustive>).

Cartes adds his decision was informed by Pope Francis's call for peace and dialogue in Paraguay following protests against this change that turned violent two weeks ago.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-paraguay-politics-idUSKBN17J1H0>); [Vatican Radio](<http://en.radiovaticana.va/news/2017/04/02/pope_appeals_for_colombia,_drc,_venezuela_and_paraguay/1302930>).

Context: Yes California.

**Archived source account.** The bid for California independence ends.

Source citations (as archived): [Business Insider](<http://www.businessinsider.com/calexit-leader-louis-marinelli-russia-2017-4>).

<a id="event-2017-04-17-4-4"></a>

Context: Palestinian prisoners of Israel.

**Archived source account.** Hundreds of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails — activists say up to 1,500 are participating — begin an open-ended hunger strike to protest poor conditions and the Israeli policy of detention without trial.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-palestinians-prisoners-idUSKBN17J0XZ>).

<a id="event-2017-04-17-4-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** Bongbong Marcos pays ₱36 million, half of the required amount to hold a recount against Philippine vice president Leni Robredo.

Source citations (as archived): [Philippine Daily Inquirer](<http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/889815/bongbong-marcos-pays-p36-m-first-installment-of-poll-protest-fee>).

#### Arts and culture

<a id="event-2017-04-18-0-0"></a>

#### Disasters and accidents

#### Law and crime

<a id="event-2017-04-18-3-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Supreme Court of the United States refuses to vacate a stay of execution issued by the Arkansas Supreme Court. Arkansas's highest court has also put on hold the execution of another inmate, Bruce Ward. The state had planned to execute eight inmates in eleven days. That schedule, as well as the use of the drug midazolam, sparked a broad range of legal challenges and humanitarian concerns about the executions. Today's planned execution of Don W. Davis would have been the state's first since 2005.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://www.cnn.com/2017/04/17/us/arkansas-executions/index.html>); [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2017/04/17/us/mondays-arkansas-execution-halted-by-state-justices.html>).
